architectureDecisions: D1 — Files: new packages/agentic-system/src/supervised-durable.js and test/bb121-supervised-durable.test.js; index.js exports createSupervisedBackendWorker. Only the three declared Living docs may also change. Existing fake-agent.mjs, crash-supervised.mjs and agent-tools/test/scope-audit.mjs are read-only fixtures/helpers. No workflow or default BackendWorker edits.

D2 — createSupervisedBackendWorker({ tool, repositoryRoot, verifications, prompt, model, maxAttempts, timeoutMs, maxFeedbackChars, permissionProfile, env, recoveryDir, eventSinks, tracer, invocationObserver }) returns frozen { execute(order, context), recover(order, context) }. execute dynamically imports ./supervised-backend.js and delegates the exact order/context and configured options to runSupervisedBackendWork; return its parsed BackendWorkResult. Never call createBackendWorker. Omitted/null recoveryDir preserves default disposal. Empty/whitespace/non-string recoveryDir throws TypeError at construction. A nonempty directory is resolved once and is dedicated to one task lineage; callers use different directories for later tasks/remediation.

D3 — Persist prerequisite: delivered BB-100 ignores recoveryDir and creates no handle. BB-142 owns adding execute forwarding into runSupervisedTask; BB-121 must not duplicate that adapter change or invoke a fresh supervisor directly during execute. After BB-142 is DONE, execute forwards recoveryDir to that delivered adapter. Worker start must prove the delivered seam persists handle.json and refuses HANDLE_CURRENT before dispatch; absence is a plan/input blocker. Do not claim durable factory execution from externally preseeded handles alone.

D4 — Recover imports mapBackendOrderToAgentTask from ./supervised-backend.js, and readAgentToolRunHandle/verifyAgentToolRunHandle/RecoveryError/reopenRecoverableWorkspace from ../../agent-tools/src/recovery.js plus resumeSupervisedTask from supervisor.js using dynamic leaf imports. Build the original task from order/context and the same configured repositoryRoot, prompt and verifications. Read recoveryDir/handle.json and verify digest; require resolved recoveryDir/repositoryRoot, taskId, baseRevision and tool.id to match. No directory or missing/malformed handle returns { action: BackendRecoveryAction.BLOCKED, result: null, blockers: [code] }; omitted directory uses SUPERVISED_RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE, invalid handle preserves HANDLE_INVALID. Revalidate disk digest immediately before use; known RecoveryError codes are BLOCKED, other execution errors propagate for durable workflow recovery. Never return RETRY_EXECUTION or silently start a new lineage.

D5 — RUNNING handles call resumeSupervisedTask(handle, { tool, task, model, maxAttempts, timeoutMs, maxFeedbackChars, permissionProfile, env, eventSinks, tracer, invocationObserver }); undefined settings preserve supervisor defaults and handle.maxAttempts. Recovery returns { action: BackendRecoveryAction.COMPLETED, result: BackendWorkResultSchema.parse(projectedResult), blockers: [] } for APPLIED, FAILED or TOOL_UNAVAILABLE/BLOCKED results. Failures to validate/reopen resume identity return BLOCKED recovery with null result. BackendRecoveryAction.COMPLETED means recovery finished; BackendWorkStatus determines success. Keep handle/Core session/worktree/tool session; never dispose the durable handle/worktree automatically, because Board checkpoint publication can still fail. Caller owns explicit disposeRecoverableRun after accepted checkpoint.

D6 — Terminal replay: resumeSupervisedTask refuses HANDLE_COMPLETE, so recover handles terminal status without calling resume or execute. Verify latest disk digest, task/tool identity, source HEAD == handle.sourceHead and registered recovery worktree HEAD == handle.candidateSha before replay. ACCEPTED/ATTEMPT_COMPLETED uses candidateSha as acceptedSha and the same fresh re-grounding as D7; EXHAUSTED maps FAILED; TOOL_UNAVAILABLE maps BLOCKED with TOOL_UNAVAILABLE blocker. Invalid terminal phase/status, wrong candidate or missing worktree is BLOCKED recovery. This covers crash after supervisor acceptance but before Board records QA_PENDING and makes repeated recovery idempotent with no additional ACT.

D7 — Accepted resume/replay is never APPLIED merely from a handle or supervisor status. Implement a private projection helper in supervised-durable.js using the delivered BB-100 evidence construction as reference; do not modify supervised-backend.js. Require a 40-hex acceptedSha, git merge-base --is-ancestor order.revision acceptedSha, a nonempty git diff, and no NO_CHANGE final attempt when attempts exist. At an isolated createLocalGitWorkspace pinned to acceptedSha, run every declared createLocalCommandVerifier with its claim and requireUnchangedTree:true; all must PASS, including required TYPECHECK and TESTS claims validated by the mapper. Use createEvidenceArtifact/subjectFromValue/environmentRefFromValue/evidenceFromVerificationArtifact to construct grounded MUTATION, TYPECHECK and TESTS evidence and git:<sha>:<requiredFile> artifact refs exactly as BB-100. Failed re-ground, unverifiable SHA or unchanged tree projects FAILED with no PASS evidence. Dispose only this projection scratch worktree in finally. Preserve source HEAD, symbolic branch, branch refs and porcelain status.

D8 — Composition is dependency injection: createDurableBackendQaWorkflow and runBackendThenQaObjective remain unchanged and use the existing execute/recover contracts. Default createBackendWorker tests remain unedited. No static imports of any agent-tools module; simultaneous barrel import plus factory construction proves no cycle. Living docs describe opt-in supervised durable execution, recovery-directory ownership, caller cleanup, fail-closed behavior, default CodeAct and separate OpenHands runtime without Blackboard ids.

D9 — DB1 delegation/persist/default disposal; DB2 real FIX_FIRST durable QA_PENDING and composition QA with matching candidate handoff; DB3 TOOL_UNAVAILABLE/BLOCKED and EXHAUSTED/FAILED without QA; DB4 default worker/source guards/barrel cycle; DB5 Living/scope audit; DB6 fresh-process Board recovery, terminal replay and fail-closed cases. Explicit FAKE_AGENT_* overlay, isolated repositories/TMPDIR, source snapshots. Future DB tests are not research delivery evidence.
